text.p: The EU Telecommunications Council scheduled for May 29 has been postponed for lack of a substantive agenda, the Dutch EU presidency said on Monday.
"We were a bit workless as a Council," a Dutch official said. He said the Council could be rescheduled for sometime in June.
The ministers were hoping to tackle a European Commission proposal to amend directive 91/263/EEC on telecommunications terminal equipment, but have so far only received unofficial documents, he said.
The Commission's proposal, expected to be formally adopted within the next few weeks, aims to ease certification procedures for telecoms companies.
The May 29 date could be snatched for a Transport Council, which will meet to finalise an accord on air and road links with Switzerland if negotiations have made enough progress, the official said.

The Dutch presidency's first Telecoms Council, in March, agreed two critical measures in the EU's telecommunications liberalisation plan -- a common position on a draft directive to update rules on voice telephone service and final adoption of a draft directive setting out a regime for authorising phone companies to operate.
